title: Private Deployments: SLO & Maintenance Communications Toolkit + TF upgrade checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight toolkit for customer-facing communications, internal escalation scripts, and Terraform/upgrade notes for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Aim: produce consistent, low-friction messaging and a tight pre/post upgrade checklist engineers can copy into runbooks. NOT final legal SLA language — use legal-approved templates for contracts.

High-level SLO/SLA language (customer-friendly paragraph samples)
1) Baseline availability statement (short):
  - "Redwood Inference will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure the private deployment control plane and inference endpoints are available 99.5% monthly. Scheduled maintenance windows will be communicated in advance and are excluded from availability calculations."
2) Incident response window (ops SLA blurb):
  - "For Priority 1 incidents impacting production inference availability, Redwood will acknowledge within 15 minutes and provide updates at least every 30 minutes until mitigated."
3) Maintenance window definition (clear):
  - "A maintenance window is a planned interval where certain services may be degraded or unavailable for upgrades, security patches, or configuration changes. Customers will receive a notification at least 72 hours in advance for standard upgrades and 24 hours for minor non-impactful patches where possible."

Customer communication templates (short, copyable)
A) Initial 72-hour notice (subject line + Slack/email body)
  Subject: Planned maintenance for your Redwood private deployment — [DATE] [window]
  Body: Hi {CustomerName},

  We're planning a routine maintenance window on {DATE} between {START} and {END} {TZ}. During this time we will perform an orchestrated upgrade of the Redwood control plane and inference runtime on your reserved cluster. Expected impact: up to {X} minutes of token-serving latency increase during quick node rotations, with no persistent downtime anticipated.

  What we will do:
  - Apply critical security patches to control plane components
  - Rotate inference nodes (rolling restart) and validate KV cache priming
  - Evaluate tail latency and revert if regressions observed

  If you require a different window or blackout dates, please reply to this thread by {RESPONSE_DEADLINE}.

  Best,
  {RedwoodEngOpsContact}

B) 24-hour reminder (minimal)
  Subject: Reminder — maintenance tomorrow for your Redwood private deployment
  Body: Short reminder: maintenance on {DATE} between {START} and {END}. Expect brief request slowdowns (couple of minutes) during rolling restarts. Full details: {link-to-runbook}.

C) Post-maintenance completion note (status + CTA)
  Subject: Maintenance complete — {DATE} — Redwood private deployment
  Body: Maintenance completed at {COMPLETE_TIME}. Summary of actions: {bulleted-list-of-actions}. Observed customer impact: {none | short latency blips | outage X min}. If you see any issues, please open a ticket referencing {INCIDENT_TAG} or reply to this email.

Short status snippets for Console/Status page (1-liners)
  - Planned: "Planned maintenance in {REGION} — brief rolling restarts expected"
  - In progress: "Maintenance in progress — some requests may see transient latency"
  - Complete: "Maintenance complete — normal service resumed"

Slack/webhook payload example (for automated channels)
  {
    "text": "[PD-MAINT] {CustomerName} — maintenance starting {DATE} {START} {TZ}. Rolling restart of inference nodes. Expected brief latency increases.",
    "attachments": [
      {"title": "Runbook", "title_link": "{runbook_url}"},
      {"title": "Contact", "text": "{oncall_name} — PagerDuty: {pd_link}"}
    ]
  }
(Note: keep webhook payloads < 8KB; prefer short attachments linking to details.)

Terraform module notes (practical pointers to include in TF modules and upgrade playbooks)
  - Module versioning: add module_version outputs and a "last_applied_manifest" tag on the stateful resources so upgrades can verify drift: e.g., output "module_version = \"v1.12.0\"" as part of the module outputs.
  - Immutable naming: prefer immutable pod/node naming for inference instances (append build metadata to resource tags) to make rollbacks easier.
  - Upgrade toggle: include a boolean var enable_in_place_upgrade = true/false. If false, run upgrade using blue/green approach to avoid in-place risky patches.
  - Terraform snippet (example to add to module outputs):
    output "module_version" {
      description = "Semantic version of the TF module used to manage this deployment"
      value       = var.module_version
    }

  - State change review: add a pre-apply hook that runs `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json` and then a small script to assert no more than N nodes replaced unless a `--force` flag is set.

Pre-upgrade runbook checklist (engineer copy-paste)
  1) Verify customer blackout windows and approvals (tickets/SC).
  2) Confirm backup snapshot exists (control plane config + model artifacts). Snapshot ID: ______.
  3) Verify Terraform plan is green and has been reviewed (link to PR).
  4) Ensure autoscaling and healthchecks are temporarily disabled for rolling operations.
  5) Prepare canary cluster (if blue/green): spin a canary with new runtime for 30 minutes. Run smoke tests.
  6) Communicate 72h and 24h notices to customer and CS.
  7) Put oncall in the loop and confirm escalation contacts.

During maintenance steps (short runbook)
  - Start at T0: notify channels "maintenance starting".
  - T0+5m: run infra preflight script: `scripts/upgrade/preflight.sh {env}`
  - T0+15m: apply terraform plan for control plane changes. Observe resource changes.
  - For each inference node rotation: wait for health endpoint to return 200 and KV cache to prime (check logs for "kv_cache_ready").
  - If any node takes > 10 minutes to become healthy, pause; run `kubectl logs` and escalate to oncall.

Rollback and emergency abort (explicit)
  - Abort rule: if customer-facing latency > 3x baseline for > 10 minutes during a rotation OR total downstream request failure rate > 1% for > 5 minutes, start rollback.
  - Quick rollback steps:
    1) Set traffic routing to previous control-plane variant (if using blue/green).
    2) If in-place: use terraform to revert to last-known-good state: `terraform apply -var-file=last-known-good.tfvars` (only after CI-validated plan).
    3) Re-enable autoscaling/rewind any temporary config changes.
    4) Notify customer (immediate) and begin postmortem capture.

Post-maintenance validation (automated and manual)
  - Automated smoke tests (copyable bash):
    # smoke.sh
    curl -sS -X POST {endpoint}/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' | jq '.status'
  - Run a small token-latency sweep: 10 requests across 3 regions, record p50/p95.
  - Verify telemetry: no new error classes in logs, token cost within expected variance.

Customer-facing escalation flow (who to contact)
  - Primary: Customer Success (name/email)
  - Ops escalation: EngOps oncall (PagerDuty link)
  - Product/security if data-access or config drift observed.
  - Template subject for urgent items: "Urgent: {CustomerName} — maintenance rollback initiated — action required"

Notes to self / unresolved items (working doc bits)
  - Decide default SLA wording for minor non-disruptive patches (72h vs 24h notice).
  - Add a short checkbox to TF modules to mark whether the module "touches data-plane" vs "control-plane". Impact-based notice rules should derive from that flag.
  - Consider an automated health-check endpoint that returns a single JSON blob with "kv_cache_ready" and "model_warm" to speed validations.

Example short postmortem blurb for customers (1–2 paragraphs)
  "Summary: During scheduled maintenance on {DATE}, we performed a rolling upgrade of the inference runtime. Impact: brief latency spikes observed affecting a subset of requests; no lost data. Root cause: higher-than-expected cache warm time on node type X. Resolution: we rolled back the node to the previous runtime and implemented a pre-warm step in the upgrade plan. Next steps: include pre-warm in future runs and adjust the default rolling window by +5 minutes."

Final checklist (copy for ticket template)
  - [ ] Customer approval recorded
  - [ ] Backups/snapshots created (IDs)
  - [ ] TF plan approved and PR linked
  - [ ] Oncall notified and escalation contacts validated
  - [ ] 72h notice sent
  - [ ] 24h reminder sent
  - [ ] Canary smoke tests pass
  - [ ] Maintenance executed and monitored
  - [ ] Post-maintenance tests pass
  - [ ] Customer notified and ticket closed

Tagging guidance for events and tickets
  - Use tags: pd-maint, pd-upgrade, pd-rollback, pd-slo, pd-incident to help metrics and filter retro queries.

If anything in this doc looks useful to be added to the canonical runbooks, copy into Confluence and link PRs back here. — Marta
